subject: Agriculture
title: The Tractor Age
description: Learn The Tractor Age in one minute.

hook.text: In 1900, a farmer fed 7 people. By 1990, tractors helped a single farmer feed 130. Machines changed everything.

buildup.text: Early tractors were steam-powered and massive. The Fordson tractor of 1917 made mechanization affordable.

discovery.text: Tractors replaced 22 million horses and mules in the US—and freed 70 million acres of farmland that fed those animals.

twist.text: Tractors favored large farms. Mechanization drove millions of small farmers off the land and into cities.

climax.text: In sub-Saharan Africa, 80% of farmland is still cultivated by hand. Mechanization's revolution hasn't reached everyone.

punchline.text: One tractor replaces 100 workers. Progress for the farm—displacement for the farmer.

quiz.question: How many people could one farmer feed by 1990 thanks to mechanization?
